thread:
morgan: Morning async check — quick ops scrub. What I did: deployed the alert filter for near-duplicate token spikes and pushed the caching tweak to staging. Blocker: still seeing intermittent 503s from dedupe-service under burst load. Today: triage runbook, coordinate canary/revert, and update SLO notes. @kevin are you oncall?
julia: Deploy SHA for the change is abc1234 (rolled at 02:45). I can roll back if we decide. Saw nginx upstream timeouts in the shard logs.
pagerbot: pagerbot: Alert fired 03:12 UTC - dedupe-service 503 spike (50m window). Page routed to @kevin.
kevin: Oncall here — acked the page and looking at logs now. Can someone confirm the last deploy SHA (thx julia).
julia: confirming: abc1234. Also grabbing the nginx tail now. snippet: ```tail -n 80 /var/log/nginx/dedupe-access.log | grep 503 | tail -n 20```
sam: I suspect KV cache thrash after the config change — saw mem pressure on node-7 in staging. Reverting the config in staging returned latencies to normal. Recommend reverting prod change or at least canary with smaller traffic + bump batch window to 40ms. Command I'd run: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/dedupe-service -n prod --to-revision=3`
morgan: Can we do a canary revert to 2 pods first and monitor p99 and error rate? @ana can you coordinate the canary steps and hold the rollback until we confirm? SLO dashboard shows p99 latency breached twice in the last hour.
ana: on it — will run the canary revert now. Plan: scale down to 2 replicas on the canary subset then `kubectl rollout undo` for that subset, validate, then roll forward. Adding note to runbook about connection pool sizing. Will update in 10m :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
kevin: tailing app logs shows repeated `ERROR: kv fetch timeout 500ms` which matches the thrash theory. Quick mitigation: increase nginx upstream timeout to 800ms on canary and monitor. Pushing the nginx change to canary now.
julia: filing a follow-up ticket to add backpressure metrics and an alert for kv latency > 300ms for 5m. Will link the ticket here when created.
morgan: good. If canary revert is green, we can schedule full rollback in the next deploy window and capture the postmortem. Ticket id (placeholder): INF-4721 — assign to @sam. Any blockers for that @sam?
sam: No blockers, will own the rollback and draft a short blameless postmortem after incident closes. I'll include SLO impact and suggested mitigations.
pagerbot: pagerbot: Incident resolved at 03:28 UTC — alert auto-closed after error rate returned to baseline. Logs archived to /var/log/incidents/1945678910.log.
morgan: Thanks all — please add any lingering follow-ups to INF-4721 and react with :+1: when done. I’ll fold SLO impact into the weekly reliability report.
